Let's step this up.

Where does socialism currently exist in the United States?

What socialist proposals has Bernie made?

Which of those would or could actually be implemented?

Believe it or not, the current system Americans live in is by definition a social (as in socialist) democracy. The problem with and unfortunate downfall of having conversations like these on forums like this is that the words "socialism," "communism" (which people erroneously associate with socialism), "libertarianism," etc, are much to charged to the American populace and without fail you'll get someone misusing them and derailing the discussion. You have no idea how badly I want to have an open discussion on these things but can't because of who I would be having it with.

Every definition is going to be "slippery" since it's not like there is an official definition of socialism any more than there's an official definition of capitalism. It means different things to different people. And while there are right and wrong definitions, there is also a lot of grey as you transition between them. One critical thing is that communism and socialism are radically different. The difference there is some order of magnitudes greater than the difference between socialism and capitalism. This is important as the history of the United States along with a very pro-capitalist push from the government has resulted in many people conflating the two.

In general the most basic premise of socialism is that individuals are still rewarded according to their merit - as in capitalism, but without the implicit punishment of those who fail to provide much merit. You're not going to starve or go without healthcare or a roof over your head in socialism. Another major difference is that in a socialist country companies operating a public need are generally publicly owned with the profits from that endeavor fed back into the country instead of going to a handful of privileged owners. So for instance instead of having Comcast and Time Warner with a coercive monopoly making a tiny handful of billionaires even bigger billionaires, you would have a public monopoly with every citizen by birth being an effective shareholder.

Communism is an altogether different beast. Individuals are no longer rewarded according to merit. The ideal there is to entirely do away with the concept of ownership and even money. There no longer is even anything such as a reward per se. Everything is government owned and equally distributed in a share they decide upon.

Abbreviated definitions by analogy.

Capitalism - I hope you like the situation you happened to born into because that's all you're getting. Now go out there and try to earn even more!

Socialism - Here's $30,000 a year to use to cover your basic needs. I'll also give you free healthcare and basic modern necessities like internet. Now go out there and try to earn even more!

Communism - Welcome to existence. Here is a yearly voucher for one standard housing unit, 300 tomatoes, 900 potatoes, 2 pigs, and a bicycle. Work hard, give us everything you earn, and next year everybody might get 310 tomatoes instead!

Something that ignorant (sorry not sorry) Americans will argue about ad nauseam.
